purpose: Synthetic full CIPL triple (B/L+PL+Invoice), deliberately inconsistent on 4 points - one for each rejection cause named in the Executive Summary: HS code error, CIF inconsistency, NIB/NPWP format failure, cross-document (package count) mismatch. Everything else is kept correct/consistent so each failure signal is isolated.

deliberate_failures.detail: B/L header states 500 CTNS, but the Packing List line items sum to 480 CTNS.
Invoice states CIF USD 12,500.00, but FOB+freight+insurance computes to USD 14,618.00 (14.5% difference, exceeds 5% tolerance).
HS code printed as '731990' (6 digits) instead of the required 8-digit BTKI code.
Importer NIB printed as '812001234567' (12 digits) instead of the required 13 digits.

cross_document_validation.name: Gross weight tolerance 2% (B/L vs sum PL items)
cross_document_validation.note: kept matching on purpose to isolate the CV001 count-only failure

cross_document_validation.name: NPWP checksum valid
cross_document_validation.result: PASS (format only, not a real checksum)

cross_document_validation.name: Line item count consistency (PL vs invoice, <=1 diff)
Vessel name consistency B/L vs AIS

expected_ceisa_simulator_result.scenario: S06 (Mixed Realistic) or a custom scenario
expected_ceisa_simulator_result.note: Pre-submit checklist (F-020) requires ALL CRITICAL rules to pass before submission - CV001, CV006 and CV008 are CRITICAL here, so this declaration should be BLOCKED at the Human Review step and never even reach the CEISA simulator, unless the pipeline has a bug.

notes: SYNTHETIC DATA - no real company, NIB, or NPWP. Safe to redistribute for testing/training.
Gross weight (CV005) and currency/line-item count (CV004/CV010) were kept CONSISTENT on purpose, so this fixture isolates exactly 4 failure signals instead of failing everything at once.
Use this alongside CIPL_HappyPath_CDP_01 as a minimal contrastive pair: same document structure, opposite outcome.
